title: implement 2D convolutions

atoms.evidence: oh = 1 + (h - kh) // stride_h; ow = 1 + (w - kw) // stride_w — 2D version of full formula
x_strided = x_padded.as_strided(size=(b, ic, oh, ow, kh, kw), stride=(s_b, s_ic, s_h * stride_h, s_w * stride_w, s_h, s_w))
einops.einsum(x_strided, weights, 'b ic oh ow kh kw, oc ic kh kw -> b oc oh ow')
full 2D version of strided-window conv with stride + padding
x_padded = pad2d(x, left=padding_w, right=padding_w, top=padding_h, bottom=padding_h, pad_value=0)
stride_h, stride_w handled via force_pair; new strides scale by stride_h/stride_w for the output-position dims
weights: Float[Tensor, 'out_channels in_channels kernel_height kernel_width'] — the (oc, ic, kH, kW) layout

notes: 9-atom exercise (tied with BatchNorm2d for densest) — the full from-scratch 2D conv. force_pair (int-or-tuple normalization) is a small utility helper but not its own atom — it could become one (`int-or-pair-helper`) if it recurs in 0_2_23 maxpool2d. All 4 conv-mechanics + stride + windowing + channel-sum + output-shape all fire together — this exercise is the convergence point of the strided-conv track.
